knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)

library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

```{r ui}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Toffoletto_2023_dexamethasone_rabbit"))
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-023-03560-7> (open access; PMC10447275)
* Supplement: Electronic Supplementary Material 1 (Supplementary Figs. S1-S2,
  Supplementary Table S1), available from the article page.

Toffoletto et al. built a physiology-based ocular model to follow a drug from a
therapeutic soft contact lens into the tear film, the sclera and choroid, the
retina, the vitreous humour and the aqueous humour. Transport across each
barrier is the exposed area times the barrier permeability times the difference
of the partition-corrected concentrations (Eqs. 2-6). The general form treats
the lens as a diffusion slab (Eq. 1, a partial differential equation in the
lens thickness). For the only time-course data available, the dexamethasone
sandwich lens of Ross et al. (2019), release is governed by polymer degradation
rather than diffusion, so the authors replaced the lens equation by the
measured in-vitro release, `R = M_Released / T * exp(-t/T)` (Eqs. 12-13), of
which a fraction `F` crosses the cornea into the aqueous humour and the rest
enters the tears (Eqs. 10-11). That validated form is the one packaged here.
The lens is a `depot` dosed with the released amount `M_Released`; first-order
release from it with rate constant `ka = 1/T` reproduces Eq. 13 exactly.

# Population

The model was not fitted to animals. Its anatomy (Table II) and physiology
(Table IV) are literature values for the rabbit eye, and its drug-specific
inputs (Table III) are literature permeabilities and partition coefficients for
dexamethasone, two of them (`K_ScCh`, `K_Ret`) adjusted by hand during the
validation. It was compared against the rabbit data of Ross et al. (2019),
who measured dexamethasone in the aqueous humour, choroid, sclera, retina and
vitreous humour at 0.25, 1, 2, 5 and 7 days of wearing the lens (3-5 eyes per
time point in Fig. 3 of Toffoletto 2023). The model describes one eye.

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

## Digitised reference values

The paper prints neither the lens release constants nor any numerical
concentrations, so the maintainers digitised the figures. The release curve
of Supplementary Fig. S1 (the exponential fit of Eq. 12, drawn dashed over the
in-vitro data) gives `M_Released = 1.047e6 ng` and `T = 2.55 days`. The model
curves of Fig. 3 (log scale) and Fig. 5 (linear scale, the same simulation)
give the values below; the tear curve of Fig. 5 is a single exponential,
`89,200 * exp(-t / 2.513 days)` ng/mL.

```{r digitised}
fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~tissue,            ~time, ~conc,
  "Aqueous humour",     0.5, 1140,
  "Aqueous humour",     1.5,  771,
  "Aqueous humour",     3.0,  419,
  "Aqueous humour",     4.0,  284,
  "Aqueous humour",     6.0,  130,
  "Aqueous humour",     8.0,   59.4,
  "Sclera-choroid",     0.15, 620,
  "Sclera-choroid",     4.0,  136,
  "Sclera-choroid",     6.0,   62.0,
  "Sclera-choroid",     8.0,   28.4,
  "Retina",             0.5,  376,
  "Retina",             1.5,  419,
  "Retina",             3.0,  272,
  "Retina",             4.0,  192,
  "Retina",             6.0,   87.8,
  "Retina",             8.0,   40.2,
  "Vitreous humour",    0.5,   30.3,
  "Vitreous humour",    1.5,   41.9,
  "Vitreous humour",    3.0,   28.4,
  "Vitreous humour",    4.0,   20.0,
  "Vitreous humour",    6.0,    9.17,
  "Vitreous humour",    8.0,    4.19
)
tear_fig5 <- function(t) 89200 * exp(-t / 2.513)
```

# Simulation

One eye wearing the lens; the dose is the total amount released in vitro.
Observation rows sit on the `tear` state; rxode2 returns every concentration
output on each row.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Toffoletto_2023_dexamethasone_rabbit")
m_released_ug <- 1047

times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 0.5, by = 0.01), seq(0.5, 12, by = 0.05), fig3$time)))
events <- rxode2::et(amt = m_released_ug, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(time = times, cmt = "tear")

sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12))
if (is.null(sim$id)) sim$id <- 1L

tissue_cols <- c(
  Tears = "Ctear",
  "Aqueous humour" = "Caqueous_humour",
  "Sclera-choroid" = "Csclera_choroid",
  Retina = "Cretina",
  "Vitreous humour" = "Cvitreous"
)
sim_long <- sim |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, dplyr::all_of(unname(tissue_cols))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(id, time), names_to = "output", values_to = "Cc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(tissue = names(tissue_cols)[match(output, tissue_cols)])
```

## Lens release

The depot reproduces the release fit of Supplementary Fig. S1 by construction:
the cumulative amount released is `M_Released * (1 - exp(-t/T))`.

```{r release}
rel <- sim |> dplyr::mutate(released_ng = 1000 * (m_released_ug - depot))
stopifnot(
  max(abs(rel$released_ng - 1.047e6 * (1 - exp(-rel$time / 2.55)))) < 1
)
ggplot(rel |> dplyr::filter(time <= 7), aes(time, released_ng)) +
  geom_line(linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Cumulative drug release (ng)",
    caption = "Replicates the dashed fit of Supplementary Fig. S1 (right panel) of Toffoletto 2023."
  )
```

ggplot(sim_long, aes(time, Cc, colour = tissue)) +

    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Toffoletto 2023 (main panel)."

ggplot(sim_long |> dplyr::filter(tissue != "Tears"), aes(time, Cc, colour = tissue)) +

## Figure 3: comparison with the published model curves

The packaged model (solid) against the model curves digitised from Fig. 3
(points). The tear film and the aqueous humour agree; the sclera-choroid,
retina and vitreous do not (see *Known discrepancy* below). The dashed curves
show the alternative reading of Eq. 3 described there.

```{r figure-3}
# Alternative reading of Eq. 3: choroidal clearance acting on the
# partition-corrected concentration C_ScCh / K_ScCh, like every other
# outflow term of the sclera-choroid balance.
mod_alt <- rxode2::rxode(mod) |>
  rxode2::model(
    d/dt(sclera_choroid) <- q_uv * c_aq - q_uv * c_sc / kp_sclera_choroid +
      flux_bulbar - cl_sc * c_sc / kp_sclera_choroid - flux_rpe
  )
sim_alt <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_alt, events, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12))
if (is.null(sim_alt$id)) sim_alt$id <- 1L
sim_alt_long <- sim_alt |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, dplyr::all_of(unname(tissue_cols))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(id, time), names_to = "output", values_to = "Cc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(tissue = names(tissue_cols)[match(output, tissue_cols)])

fig3_tissues <- c("Aqueous humour", "Sclera-choroid", "Retina", "Vitreous humour")
ggplot(
  sim_long |> dplyr::filter(tissue %in% fig3_tissues, time >= 0.01, time <= 8),
  aes(time, Cc)
) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = "Eq. 3 as printed (packaged)")) +
  geom_line(
    data = sim_alt_long |> dplyr::filter(tissue %in% fig3_tissues, time >= 0.01, time <= 8),
    aes(linetype = "Clearance on C_ScCh / K_ScCh")
  ) +
  geom_point(data = fig3, aes(time, conc), colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~tissue) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1, 1e4)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Drug concentration (ng/g tissue)", linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Toffoletto 2023; red points are its model curves, digitised."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Quantitative checks

All checks below are deterministic (the model has no random effects), so
their bounds only need to cover the digitisation error of the figures (a few
percent).

```{r checks}
at <- function(d, tis, t) {
  v <- d$Cc[d$tissue == tis & abs(d$time - t) < 1e-9]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique simulated row for ", tis, " at ", t)
  v
}
cmp <- fig3 |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    printed = at(sim_long, tissue, time),
    alternative = at(sim_alt_long, tissue, time)
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ratio_printed = printed / conc,
    ratio_alternative = alternative / conc
  )
cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Tissue = tissue, "Time (day)" = time, "Fig. 3 (ng/g)" = conc,
    "Packaged model" = printed, "Alternative Eq. 3" = alternative,
    "Packaged / Fig. 3" = ratio_printed, "Alternative / Fig. 3" = ratio_alternative
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated concentrations against the digitised Fig. 3 model curves.")

tear_ratio <- sapply(c(1, 4, 8), function(t) at(sim_long, "Tears", t) / tear_fig5(t))
tear_ratio

stopifnot(
  # Tears: the release constants and the tear outflows (Q_Drain, P_Conj x
  # A_Palp, P_Conj x A_Bulb) set this level. Measured 1.03, 1.05, 1.08 at
  # days 1, 4, 8: the Fig. 5 curve decays with T = 2.51 days against the
  # 2.55 days of Supplementary Fig. S1, so the ratio drifts up with time.
  all(abs(tear_ratio - 1) < 0.10),
  # Aqueous humour: F, Q_Aq and the release; measured 1.04-1.06.
  all(abs(cmp$ratio_printed[cmp$tissue == "Aqueous humour"] - 1) < 0.15)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA on each output, grouped by tissue. The paper reports no NCA table; the
reference values are the peaks digitised from Fig. 5 and, for the aqueous
humour, the area under the exponential fit of Supplementary Fig. S1
(`1636.7 * exp(-5e-6 t)`, t in seconds), which the authors used in Eq. 14 to
derive `F`: 1636.7 / 5e-6 ng s/mL = 3789 ng day/mL.

```{r pknca}
conc_nca <- sim_long |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, tissue)
stopifnot(all(conc_nca$time[!duplicated(conc_nca[, c("id", "tissue")])] == 0))

dose_nca <- conc_nca |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, tissue) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = m_released_ug)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_nca, Cc ~ time | tissue + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | tissue + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

reference <- tibble::tribble(
  ~tissue,            ~PPTESTCD,    ~PPORRES,
  "Tears",            "cmax",       89200,
  "Tears",            "half.life",  2.513 * log(2),
  "Aqueous humour",   "cmax",       1234,
  "Aqueous humour",   "tmax",       0.22,
  "Aqueous humour",   "aucinf.obs", 1636.7 / 5e-6 / 86400,
  "Sclera-choroid",   "cmax",       611,
  "Retina",           "cmax",       447,
  "Retina",           "tmax",       1.02,
  "Vitreous humour",  "cmax",       42,
  "Vitreous humour",  "tmax",       1.18
)

nca_cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = reference,
  by = "tissue",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "day", aucinf.obs = "ng*day/mL", half.life = "day"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  nca_cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated vs. digitised published values (Fig. 5 peaks; Supplementary",
    "Fig. S1 aqueous AUC). * differs by more than 20 percent."
  )
)
```

The tear film and aqueous humour agree within a few percent, including the
aqueous-humour AUC that the authors used to derive `F` (`F = Q_Aq x AUC /
M_Released`): the simulated AUC is about 5 percent below the Supplementary
Fig. S1 value, consistent with the one-significant-figure rate constant
(`5E-06`) printed on that fit. The sclera-choroid, retina and vitreous peaks are
starred; see below.

# Known discrepancy: sclera-choroid, retina and vitreous

Eq. 3 removes drug from the sclera-choroid by choroidal blood flow as
`Clearance_ScCh x C_ScCh`, with `Clearance_ScCh = 1 mL/min` (Table IV). Solved
as printed, the sclera-choroid concentration is about 16 times below the
paper's own Fig. 3 and Fig. 5 curves, and the retina and vitreous (fed from the
sclera-choroid) are 20-35 times below. Every other outflow of the
sclera-choroid balance acts on the partition-corrected concentration
`C_ScCh / K_ScCh`; applying the choroidal clearance to that concentration as
well (equivalently, a clearance of 1/15 mL/min on `C_ScCh`) reproduces the
published sclera-choroid curve within about 6 percent, but still leaves the
retina and vitreous at 0.5-0.7 times the published curves. No single
reading of the printed equations and tables reproduces all five published
curves, so the package keeps Eq. 3 and Table IV exactly as printed; the
alternative reading is shown above for comparison. The checks below pin both
behaviours so that any later change to the model has to revisit this section.

```{r discrepancy}
r <- function(col, tis) cmp[[col]][cmp$tissue == tis]
stopifnot(
  # As printed: sclera-choroid ratios measured 0.06; retina 0.03-0.05;
  # vitreous 0.03-0.05.
  all(r("ratio_printed", "Sclera-choroid") < 0.2),
  all(r("ratio_printed", "Retina") < 0.2),
  all(r("ratio_printed", "Vitreous humour") < 0.2),
  # Alternative reading: sclera-choroid measured 0.94-0.96; retina and
  # vitreous measured 0.50-0.73.
  all(abs(r("ratio_alternative", "Sclera-choroid") - 1) < 0.2),
  all(r("ratio_alternative", "Retina") < 0.85),
  all(r("ratio_alternative", "Vitreous humour") < 0.85)
)
```

# Other drugs (Supplementary Table S1)

The authors also compared the model with single-study data for melatonin,
dexamethasone (Bengani 2020 lens), latanoprost, ofloxacin and pravastatin
(Fig. 4), changing only the drug- and lens-specific inputs of Supplementary
Table S1. The release constants of those lenses (`M_Released`, `T`, or the
diffusion-lens inputs `D_SCL`, `H`, `K_SCL`) are not reported, so those
scenarios cannot be reproduced here; the drug inputs can be swapped into the
packaged model with `rxode2::ini()` once a release profile is available.

```{r table-s1}
table_s1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug,                          ~p_conj, ~p_rpe, ~p_ilm, ~kp_sclera_choroid, ~kp_retina, ~f_aqueous_humour,
  "Dexamethasone (Bengani 2020)", 2.5e-6,  10e-6,  13e-6,  15,                 10,         0.0349,
  "Melatonin",                    2.5e-6,  10e-6,  13e-6,  15,                 10,         0.0293,
  "Latanoprost",                  3.0e-6,  10e-6,  13e-6,  17,                 11,         0.0208,
  "Ofloxacin",                    2.5e-7,   5e-6,   7e-6,   7,                  5,         0.0707,
  "Pravastatin",                  2.5e-7,   3e-6,   4e-6,   3,                  3,         0.0787
)
table_s1 |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(p_conj, p_rpe, p_ilm), function(x) formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 1))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Supplementary Table S1 drug-specific inputs (permeabilities in cm/s).")

# Example: the ofloxacin inputs, ready for a user-supplied release profile.
mod_oflox <- rxode2::rxode(mod) |>
  rxode2::ini(
    p_conj = 2.5e-7, p_rpe = 5e-6, p_ilm = 7e-6,
    kp_sclera_choroid = 7, kp_retina = 5, f_aqueous_humour = 0.0707
  )
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(mod_oflox$theta["kp_retina"]), 5)))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Release constants digitised.** `M_Released` and `T` are not printed. The
  maintainers digitised the dashed exponential fit of Supplementary Fig. S1
  (right panel) and fitted Eq. 12 to the digitised curve: `M_Released =
  1.047e6 ng`, `T = 2.55 days`. Two independent checks agree: the tear curve
  of Fig. 5 decays with a time constant of 2.51 days, and the tear and
  aqueous-humour levels it implies are within 2-8 percent of the simulation.
  Using the 7-day in-vitro total of about 1.1e6 ng instead reproduces the
  printed `F = 2.08` percent more closely through Eq. 14, so the released
  amount is uncertain by about 5 percent.
- **`F` for the Ross 2019 lens.** Table III gives `F = 2.08` percent for this
  data set, while Supplementary Table S1 gives 3.49 percent for the Bengani
  2020 dexamethasone lens and 2.08 percent for latanoprost. The Table III value
  is used here; the Bengani value belongs to a different lens.
- **Sclera-choroid clearance kept as printed.** See *Known discrepancy*. The
  printed Eq. 3 and Table IV value under-predict the published sclera-choroid,
  retina and vitreous curves; the alternative reading is shown but not
  packaged.
- **Corneal epithelium not included.** Eq. 7 needs the partition coefficients
  `K_Ep/Aq` and `K_Ep/t`, which the paper does not report; the
  corneal-epithelium concentration is therefore not an output.
- **Diffusion-lens form not included.** Eqs. 1, 2, 6, 8 and 9 describe
  diffusion through the lens thickness (a partial differential equation). The
  paper gives no lens diffusivity, thickness or lens partition coefficient,
  and its validation uses the release-rate form instead.
- **`K_Aq` not used.** Table IV lists `K_Aq = 1`, but it appears in none of the
  validated equations (Eqs. 3-5, 10, 11), so the model does not carry it.
- **Concentration units.** Outputs are ng/mL; the paper reports ng/g tissue,
  which is the same number at unit tissue density.
- **No variability.** The model is deterministic; the paper's uncertainty
  analysis (all inputs varied by +/-10 percent, Supplementary Fig. S2) is a
  sensitivity exercise, not an estimate of between-animal variability.
- A search for errata or corrections to Toffoletto 2023 found none as of
  2026-10-27.
